recommendations.text: Trace telemetry ingestion, ordering, and race-state updates to identify the cause of a car's laps appearing out of driving order after roughly eighteen hours of continuous operation.
Fix the identified cause so that long-running telemetry processing preserves each car's lap sequence in driving order.

Add a deterministic regression test that reproduces the identified corruption, fails on the pre-fix implementation, and passes with the fix. Exercise the relevant long-session boundary without requiring an eighteen-hour wall-clock run.
Verify that the regression test checks per-car lap order in the resulting race state, not merely an intermediate telemetry value, and that ordinary short-session ordering remains correct.
Run the reported project test command, npm test, and report the regression test's pre-fix failure and post-fix success along with any remaining test failures.

Treat the approximate eighteen-hour onset as a diagnostic clue, not proof of a specific overflow, rollover, or ordering defect; establish the cause from code and reproducible evidence before choosing the fix.
Keep changes focused on the telemetry ordering defect and its regression coverage; unrelated pipeline redesign and repair of previously corrupted race data are outside this scope.
